## Verdict: REJECT (one Important finding: a stale release-note sentence that acceptance criterion nineteen requires to be corrected before merge)
The PR is not ready to merge: an existing release-note fragment still tells users that `sqllens verify-memory` is not supported under a rule-set file, which this PR makes false, and nothing in this change or the base corrects it.
Rule applied: rule 3 — a Phase-3 finding at or above the threshold (important) → REJECT

## Code Review Findings
### 🟠 Important / Major
1. `changelog.d/389.added.md` line 10 still says "`sqllens verify-memory` is not supported". After this PR, that sentence is false, and it contradicts the new `changelog.d/400.added.md`. Acceptance criterion nineteen requires the sentence to be corrected through a separate `codex/changelog-notes-<reason>` PR that merges before this one; neither the base nor the head shows that correction. (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: release-note fragment consumed into published CHANGELOG; no reader decides program behavior from it -->

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (4)
<details><summary>4 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/eval/runner.py` lines 120-180: `VerificationIdentityError.kind` is a plain `str`, and `describe()` sends any unknown kind to the `refused`/`catalog` message. The constructor does not check which fields go with which kind, for example `kind="missing"` with an empty `missing` tuple. (raised by 1/4 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/eval/runner.py` line 237: `_verification_metadata` sets `loaded.catalog.confirmed = True` outside the state lock, after `confirm_catalog` has already set it under the lock. The second write is redundant and weakens the encapsulation of `confirm_catalog`. (raised by 1/4 agents)
- VC-28: FAIL (suggestion) — The release note says a refused run stops with exit 1 naming the refusal and the values it used [changelog.d/400.added.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  changelog.d/400.added.md says a refused run stops with exit 1 'naming the refusal and the values it used'. cli.py:652-657 does exit 1 with e.describe(...). But VerificationIdentityError.describe (src/sqllens/eval/runner.py:151-176) renders the values used (rule set, account, user) only in the fall-through branch, which covers kinds refused and catalog (lines 170-176). no_rule_set_file (154-158) is a fixed string with no values; missing (159-164) names only the absent fields; account_required (165-169) is a fixed string, although rule_set and user_id are passed at runner.py:203-205 they are not rendered. So for three of five refusal kinds the message does not name the values used; the absolute wording overstates.

  </details>

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred
- VC-55: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — When this issue's PR merges, no fragment in `changelog.d/` on `main` says `sqllens verify-memory` is not supported or not available under a rule-set file. Today `changelog.d/389.added.md` says "`sqllens verify-memory` is not supported"; while that fragment is unreleased, its sentence is corrected through a `codex/changelog-notes-<reason>` PR that merges before this issue's PR. [changelog.d/400.added.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  criteria.json is a valid list and carries criterion 19, so it counts. At head 54c376c, changelog.d/389.added.md:10 still reads 'and `sqllens verify-memory` is not supported.' Grep of view-head/changelog.d for 'not supported|not available|unsupported' finds no other fragment about verify-memory (387.removed.md:8 and +legacy-001.security.md:4 are unrelated). The PR diff touches only changelog.d/400.added.md and does not edit 389.added.md. Criterion 19 says the correction comes through a separate codex/changelog-notes-<reason> PR that merges before this PR. That PR is not in either view: base 4521a6f and head both still carry the sentence. Whether it merges first cannot be shown from the source or artifacts. I did not run any check of the remote or main branch state, so the post-merge state of main stays unverified. If this PR merged now, the stale sentence would remain.

  </details>

But VerificationIdentityError.describe (src/sqllens/eval/runner.py:151-176) renders the values used (rule set, account, user) only in the fall-through branch, which covers kinds refused and catalog (lines 170-176). no_rule_set_file (154-158) is a fixed string with no values; missing (159-164) names only the absent fields; account_required (165-169) is a fixed string, although rule_set and user_id are passed at runner.py:203-205 they are not rendered. So for three of five refusal kinds the message does not name the values used; the absolute wording overstates.
